audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 10, first-pass draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for diplomatic condolence, suspicion of espionage, beard and garment humiliation, masculinity and sexual shame, mercenary armies, escalation, casualty figures, vassalage, and Divine-war rhetoric.

verses.restored: After this, king of children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And it came to pass after this, that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: Some time later, the king of the Ammonites died and was succeeded by his son Hanun.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַיָּ֕מָת מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ חָנ֥וּן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

verses.restored: David said, I will do covenant-kindness with Hanun son of Nahash, as his father did kindness with me. David sent by hand of his servants to comfort him concerning his father. David's servants came into land of children of Ammon.

familiar.text: Then said David, I will shew kindness unto Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father shewed kindness unto me. And David sent to comfort him by the hand of his servants for his father. And David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.

modern.text: And David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent some of his servants to console Hanun concerning his father. But when they arrived in the land of the Ammonites,

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶעֱשֶׂה חֶ֣סֶד עִם חָנ֣וּן בֶּן נָחָ֗שׁ כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ עָשָׂ֨ה אָבִ֤יו עִמָּדִי֙ חֶ֔סֶד וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח דָּוִ֧ד לְנַחֲמ֛וֹ בְּיַד עֲבָדָ֖יו אֶל אָבִ֑יו וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד אֶ֖רֶץ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן

verses.restored: Officials of children of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, Is David honoring your father in your eyes by sending comforters? Has David not sent his servants to search city, spy it out, and overthrow it?

familiar.text: And the princes of the children of Ammon said unto Hanun their lord, Thinkest thou that David doth honour thy father, that he hath sent comforters unto thee? hath not David rather sent his servants unto thee, to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?

modern.text: the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun their lord, “Just because David has sent you comforters, do you really believe he is showing respect for your father? Has not David instead sent his servants to explore the city, spy it out, and overthrow it?”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י בְנֵֽי עַמּ֜וֹן אֶל חָנ֣וּן אֲדֹֽנֵיהֶ֗ם הַֽמְכַבֵּ֨ד דָּוִ֤ד אֶת אָבִ֨יךָ֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי שָׁלַ֥ח לְךָ֖ מְנַֽחֲמִ֑ים הֲ֠לוֹא בַּעֲב֞וּר חֲק֤וֹר אֶת הָעִיר֙ וּלְרַגְּלָ֣הּ וּלְהָפְכָ֔הּ שָׁלַ֥ח דָּוִ֛ד אֶת עֲבָדָ֖יו אֵלֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Hanun took David's servants, shaved off half of each beard, cut their garments in middle as far as buttocks, and sent them away.

familiar.text: Wherefore Hanun took David’s servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them away.

modern.text: So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved off half of each man’s beard, cut off their garments at the hips, and sent them away.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חָנ֜וּן אֶת עַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֗ד וַיְגַלַּח֙ אֶת חֲצִ֣י זְקָנָ֔ם וַיִּכְרֹ֧ת אֶת מַדְוֵיהֶ֛ם בַּחֵ֖צִי עַ֣ד שְׁתֽוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵֽם

verses.restored: They told David, and he sent to meet them, because men were greatly humiliated. King said, Stay at Jericho until your beards grow, then return.

familiar.text: When they told it unto David, he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed: and the king said, Tarry at Jericho until your beards be grown, and then return.

modern.text: When this was reported to David, he sent messengers to meet the men, since they had been thoroughly humiliated. The king told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return.”

original.text: וַיַּגִּ֤דוּ לְדָוִד֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח לִקְרָאתָ֔ם כִּֽי הָי֥וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים נִכְלָמִ֣ים מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ שְׁב֣וּ בִֽירֵח֔וֹ עַד יְצַמַּ֥ח זְקַנְכֶ֖ם וְשַׁבְתֶּֽם

verses.restored: Children of Ammon saw that they had made themselves odious to David. They sent and hired Arameans of Beth-rehob and Zobah, twenty thousand foot soldiers, king of Maacah with one thousand, and men of Tob, twelve thousand.

familiar.text: And when the children of Ammon saw that they stank before David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Bethrehob, and the Syrians of Zoba, twenty thousand footmen, and of king Maacah a thousand men, and of Ishtob twelve thousand men.

modern.text: When the Ammonites realized that they had become a stench to David, they hired twenty thousand Aramean foot soldiers from Beth-rehob and Zoba, as well as a thousand men from the king of Maacah and twelve thousand men from Tob.

original.text: וַיִּרְאוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן כִּ֥י נִבְאֲשׁ֖וּ בְּדָוִ֑ד וַיִּשְׁלְח֣וּ בְנֵֽי עַמּ֡וֹן וַיִּשְׂכְּרוּ֩ אֶת אֲרַ֨ם בֵּית רְח֜וֹב וְאֶת אֲרַ֣ם צוֹבָ֗א עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֨לֶף֙ רַגְלִ֔י וְאֶת מֶ֤לֶךְ מַֽעֲכָה֙ אֶ֣לֶף אִ֔ישׁ וְאִ֣ישׁ ט֔וֹב שְׁנֵים עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ

verses.restored: David heard and sent Joab with all army of mighty warriors.

familiar.text: And when David heard of it, he sent Joab, and all the host of the mighty men.

modern.text: On hearing this, David sent Joab and the entire army of mighty men.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ אֶת יוֹאָ֔ב וְאֵ֥ת כָּל הַצָּבָ֖א הַגִּבֹּרִֽים

verses.restored: Children of Ammon came out and arranged battle at entrance of gate. Arameans of Zobah and Rehob, men of Tob, and Maacah were by themselves in field.

familiar.text: And the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entering in of the gate: and the Syrians of Zoba, and of Rehob, and Ishtob, and Maacah, were by themselves in the field.

modern.text: The Ammonites marched out and arrayed themselves for battle at the entrance of the city gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the open country. David Defeats Ammon and Aram (1 Chronicles 19:10–19)

original.text: וַיֵּֽצְאוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וַיַּעַרְכ֥וּ מִלְחָמָ֖ה פֶּ֣תַח הַשָּׁ֑עַר וַאֲרַ֨ם צוֹבָ֤א וּרְחוֹב֙ וְאִֽישׁ ט֣וֹב וּמַֽעֲכָ֔ה לְבַדָּ֖ם בַּשָּׂדֶֽה

verses.restored: Joab saw face of battle was against him in front and behind. He chose from all chosen men of Israel and arranged them against Arameans.

familiar.text: When Joab saw that the front of the battle was against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel, and put them in array against the Syrians:

modern.text: When Joab saw the battle lines before him and behind him, he selected some of the best men of Israel and arrayed them against the Arameans.

original.text: וַיַּ֣רְא יוֹאָ֗ב כִּֽי הָיְתָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ פְּנֵ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה מִפָּנִ֖ים וּמֵֽאָח֑וֹר וַיִּבְחַ֗ר מִכֹּל֙ בְּחוּרֵ֣י בישראל וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ לִקְרַ֥את אֲרָֽם

verses.restored: Rest of people he placed in hand of Abishai his brother, who arranged them against children of Ammon.

familiar.text: And the rest of the people he delivered into the hand of Abishai his brother, that he might put them in array against the children of Ammon.

modern.text: And he placed the rest of the forces under the command of his brother Abishai, who arrayed them against the Ammonites.

original.text: וְאֵת֙ יֶ֣תֶר הָעָ֔ם נָתַ֕ן בְּיַ֖ד אַבְשַׁ֣י אָחִ֑יו וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֕ךְ לִקְרַ֖את בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן

verses.restored: He said, If Arameans are stronger than I, you shall rescue me; if children of Ammon are stronger than you, I will go to rescue you.

familiar.text: And he said, If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me: but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I will come and help thee.

modern.text: “If the Arameans are too strong for me,” said Joab, “then you will come to my rescue. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come to your rescue.

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אִם תֶּחֱזַ֤ק אֲרָם֙ מִמֶּ֔נִּי וְהָיִ֥תָה לִּ֖י לִֽישׁוּעָ֑ה וְאִם בְּנֵ֤י עַמּוֹן֙ יֶחֱזְק֣וּ מִמְּךָ֔ וְהָלַכְתִּ֖י לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַֽ לָֽךְ

verses.restored: Be strong, and let us strengthen ourselves for our people and for cities of our Divine. May YHWH do what is good in YHWH's eyes.

familiar.text: Be of good courage, and let us play the men for our people, and for the cities of our God: and the LORD do that which seemeth him good.

modern.text: Be strong and let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. May the LORD do what is good in His sight.”

original.text: חֲזַ֤ק וְנִתְחַזַּק֙ בְּעַד עַמֵּ֔נוּ וּבְעַ֖ד עָרֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַֽיהוָ֔ה יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינָֽיו

verses.restored: Joab and people with him drew near to battle against Arameans, and they fled before him.

familiar.text: And Joab drew nigh, and the people that were with him, unto the battle against the Syrians: and they fled before him.

modern.text: So Joab and his troops advanced to fight the Arameans, who fled before him.

original.text: וַיִּגַּ֣שׁ יוֹאָ֗ב וְהָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֔וֹ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה בַּֽאֲרָ֑ם וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ מִפָּנָֽיו

verses.restored: Children of Ammon saw Arameans had fled, and they also fled before Abishai and entered city. Joab returned from children of Ammon and came to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And when the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians were fled, then fled they also before Abishai, and entered into the city. So Joab returned from the children of Ammon, and came to Jerusalem.

modern.text: When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they too fled before Abishai, and they entered the city. So Joab returned from fighting against the Ammonites and came to Jerusalem.

original.text: וּבְנֵ֨י עַמּ֤וֹן רָאוּ֙ כִּי נָ֣ס אֲרָ֔ם וַיָּנֻ֨סוּ֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י אֲבִישַׁ֔י וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ הָעִ֑יר וַיָּ֣שָׁב יוֹאָ֗ב מֵעַל֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וַיָּבֹ֖א יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: Arameans saw they were defeated before Israel and gathered themselves together.

familiar.text: And when the Syrians saw that they were smitten before Israel, they gathered themselves together.

modern.text: When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they regrouped.

original.text: וַיַּ֣רְא אֲרָ֔ם כִּ֥י נִגַּ֖ף לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּאָסְפ֖וּ יָֽחַד

verses.restored: Hadadezer sent and brought out Arameans from beyond River. They came to Helam, with Shobach commander of Hadadezer's army before them.

familiar.text: And Hadarezer sent, and brought out the Syrians that were beyond the river: and they came to Helam; and Shobach the captain of the host of Hadarezer went before them.

modern.text: Hadadezer sent messengers to bring more Arameans from beyond the Euphrates, and they came to Helam with Shobach the commander of Hadadezer’s army leading them.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח הֲדַדְעֶ֗זֶר וַיֹּצֵ֤א אֶת אֲרָם֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ מֵעֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֔ר וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ חֵילָ֑ם וְשׁוֹבַ֛ךְ שַׂר צְבָ֥א הֲדַדְעֶ֖זֶר לִפְנֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: It was told David. He gathered all Israel, crossed Jordan, and came to Helam. Arameans arranged themselves against David and fought with him.

familiar.text: And when it was told David, he gathered all Israel together, and passed over Jordan, and came to Helam. And the Syrians set themselves in array against David, and fought with him.

modern.text: When this was reported to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and went to Helam. Then the Arameans arrayed themselves against David and fought against him.

original.text: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְדָוִ֗ד וַיֶּאֱסֹ֤ף אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וַיָּבֹ֖א חֵלָ֑אמָה וַיַּעַרְכ֤וּ אֲרָם֙ לִקְרַ֣את דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּלָּחֲמ֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Arameans fled before Israel. David killed from Arameans seven hundred chariot crews and forty thousand horsemen/foot soldiers; he struck Shobach commander of army, and he died there.

familiar.text: And the Syrians fled before Israel; and David slew the men of seven hundred chariots of the Syrians, and forty thousand horsemen, and smote Shobach the captain of their host, who died there.

modern.text: But the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed seven hundred charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also struck down Shobach the commander of their army, who died there.

original.text: וַיָּ֣נָס אֲרָם֮ מִפְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיַּהֲרֹ֨ג דָּוִ֜ד מֵאֲרָ֗ם שְׁבַ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ רֶ֔כֶב וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וְאֵ֨ת שׁוֹבַ֧ךְ שַׂר צְבָא֛וֹ הִכָּ֖ה וַיָּ֥מָת שָֽׁם

verses.restored: All kings who were servants of Hadadezer saw they were defeated before Israel. They made peace with Israel and served them. Arameans feared to rescue children of Ammon again.

familiar.text: And when all the kings that were servants to Hadarezer saw that they were smitten before Israel, they made peace with Israel, and served them. So the Syrians feared to help the children of Ammon any more.

modern.text: When all the kings who were subject to Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with Israel and became subject to them. So the Arameans were afraid to help the Ammonites anymore.

original.text: וַיִּרְא֨וּ כָֽל הַמְּלָכִ֜ים עַבְדֵ֣י הֲדַדְעֶ֗זֶר כִּ֤י נִגְּפוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּשְׁלִ֥מוּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיַּֽעַבְד֑וּם וַיִּֽרְא֣וּ אֲרָ֔ם לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ ע֖וֹד אֶת בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן

translation_notes: The initial mission is diplomatic condolence; suspicion turns it into humiliation and war. Misread intentions do not make escalation inevitable.
Half-shaved beards and cut garments expose bodies and attack masculine honor. The men's shame belongs to coercive humiliation, not to their bodies, hair, nudity, sexuality, or gender expression.
The phrase that Ammon 'became odious' to David is political perception, not proof that an entire people became morally repulsive.
Hired forces and royal coalitions show war as organized labor and finance, not a simple contest of ethnic heroes.
Joab's mutual-rescue plan has tactical solidarity, but courage language must not recruit people into avoidable war or equate masculinity with violence.
Casualty numbers and the horsemen/foot-soldier textual variation require witness audit. Every number represents human death.
The final peace produces service/vassalage under Israel. It is not reconciliation between equals and should not be celebrated as benevolent empire.
safety_note: Do not use bodily humiliation to enforce masculinity, mock exposed people, or justify war. Do not turn Ammonites or Arameans into timeless enemies. The chapter records diplomatic failure, retaliation, mercenary escalation, mass death, and coerced political submission.
